title: The jukebox, seen
logline: The jukebox from the tavern's side for the first time: the machine the plaster hid for twenty years, real, chrome, a cracked light. Nine o'clock. The page can hear the Springsteen.

panels.composition: Inside the tavern, the jukebox against the wall shared with the garage: an old machine, chrome pitted, one panel's light cracked, the song list yellowed. The wall behind it plain plaster. No one at it. Nine o'clock on a clock above the bar.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, an old chrome jukebox with a cracked light panel and yellowed song list against a plain plaster wall inside a dim tavern, a clock above the bar reading nine, no people, no words
image.notes: The plaster's shape (dw_2004-03-09), seen from the other side. The song: reserved; the strip called it the Springsteen.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
